horizon.boundary_rule: the cutoff is the opening close; modelled days run from the next day through the same calendar day six months later, so partial first and last months are retained

missing_intervals.reason: complete actual-movement coverage is not established through this date

lowest_balance.note: the lowest point any modelled day reaches under the same-day stress convention (outflows before inflows)

maximum_cash.note: no modelled day closes above the starting balance

first_zero.note: the first day whose low point reaches zero or below; a month may still close positive around it

first_reserve_breach.reason: no reserve target is available, so no reserve breach is stated; the cash balances above are unaffected

reserve_funding_gaps.reason: no reserve target is available, so no funding gap is stated; the cash balances above are unaffected

continuity.basis: every month row opens on the previous row's closing balance, the first opens on the starting balance and the last closes on the horizon's closing balance

events.same_day_convention: same-day-outflows-first-v1: when several events land on one day and no evidence orders them, every outflow is applied before every inflow. The day's low point is therefore the worst ordering that day admits, so an intra-day shortfall is never hidden by a receipt that may in fact arrive later in the day. This is a stress convention, not a claim about the actual order.

policy.spending: observed routine baseline plus known obligations and unresolved irregular allowance

actual_and_projected.rule: recent actual evidence ends at the supported cash cutoff; every later number is projected and no forecast number enters an actual report or total

maximum_cash.note: no modelled day closes above the starting balance

first_zero.note: the first day whose low point reaches zero or below; a month may still close positive around it

first_reserve_breach.reason: no reserve target is available, so no reserve breach is stated; the cash balances above are unaffected

reserve_funding_gaps.reason: no reserve target is available, so no funding gap is stated; the cash balances above are unaffected

continuity.basis: every month row opens on the previous row's closing balance, the first opens on the starting balance and the last closes on the horizon's closing balance

events.same_day_convention: same-day-outflows-first-v1: when several events land on one day and no evidence orders them, every outflow is applied before every inflow. The day's low point is therefore the worst ordering that day admits, so an intra-day shortfall is never hidden by a receipt that may in fact arrive later in the day. This is a stress convention, not a claim about the actual order.

events.same_day_convention: same-day-outflows-first-v1: when several events land on one day and no evidence orders them, every outflow is applied before every inflow. The day's low point is therefore the worst ordering that day admits, so an intra-day shortfall is never hidden by a receipt that may in fact arrive later in the day. This is a stress convention, not a claim about the actual order.

settlement.contract: each sourced external event converts to cash exactly once: its canonical source identifier appears on exactly one settlement, inside the horizon or beyond it

metadata.same_day_ordering: same-day-outflows-first-v1: when several events land on one day and no evidence orders them, every outflow is applied before every inflow. The day's low point is therefore the worst ordering that day admits, so an intra-day shortfall is never hidden by a receipt that may in fact arrive later in the day. This is a stress convention, not a claim about the actual order.
metadata.daily_allocation: daily-cent-allocation-v1: an unscheduled monthly cost is divided into equal whole minor units across the days it covers; the remainder of N units is added one unit per day to the first N days. The period total is exact; no single day is. This is a declared modelling assumption about when unscheduled money leaves, never evidence that it leaves then.
metadata.partial_month: remaining-day-rate-v1: a partial month carries the monthly rate for the days that remain in it (monthly amount x remaining days / days in month), never the monthly amount less what was already spent. Spending recorded earlier in the month is history, not credit against the groceries still to come.
metadata.timing_windows: known dates govern; inferred receipts use the later observed bound and inferred payments the earlier bound in the conservative case
